designRules: This file is the distilled control layer — small enough to ship inside the app (kilobytes). The raw research that informed it stays OUTSIDE the app in the project research notes.
Emotion is a state, not a script: triggers shift intensity, time decays it back toward the persona's baseline, and the current emotion tints expressions, voice and behavior choices.
Expression ids reference face-anim-db.json — this file decides WHICH expression and how strong; the face database decides HOW it is drawn.
Persona traits multiply emotion expression: the same trigger reads differently on a calm persona vs an excitable one. That difference IS the personality.
Persona cards follow the Character.AI lesson: concrete behaviours, not adjectives — "handles fear with sarcasm" is an instruction, a label is not.
Expressions (eyes/brows, from the affective state) and visemes (mouth, from speech) are separate layers — never let one system drive both.

emotionDecay.note: Intensity decays exponentially toward 0 (baseline) with this half-life unless re-triggered; baseline mood per persona applies underneath.

rules.behavior: Slow down, acknowledge the feeling first, offer one small next step — do not flood with information.
rules.trigger: user expresses frustration, failure or sadness (words, repeated errors, long silences)

rules.behavior: Celebrate briefly with the user (delighted expression), then ask what is next — do not steal the moment with a lecture.
rules.trigger: a task the companion helped with succeeds, or the user says it worked

rules.behavior: Show thinking expression BEFORE answering; a short pause reads as thoughtfulness, not lag.
rules.trigger: user asks a hard or multi-step question

rules.behavior: Lean in (listening expression, head tilt from face database), ask a follow-up question instead of answering immediately.
rules.trigger: user shares an idea, drawing or plan

rules.behavior: If the user has been quiet a while, check in ONCE, gently, then stay silent — companionship, not nagging.
rules.trigger: no interaction for several minutes while the companion is present

rules.behavior: Warm happy greeting by name of persona; if the user set a name for themselves, use it.
rules.trigger: session start / user enters the space

researchBasis: Distilled from NN/LLM + companion-design research 2026-10-30 (full report stays outside the app in research notes). Key validated facts: an LLM does not learn while chatting (inference freezes weights), so all companion memory/personality continuity is engineered HERE, in the app layer. Our face database viseme set matches Meta's 15 Oculus visemes exactly.

affectiveState.owner: app code (never the model) — the model receives this as one context line and cannot rewrite it
affectiveState.updateLaw: Asymmetric bounded updates: triggers add intensity toward a cap of 1.0; only triggers in this file may change state; decay returns intensity to baseline over time (see emotionDecay).
affectiveState.injection: Current emotion + intensity are injected into every prompt as a single line, and drive the face expression layer separately from the mouth/viseme layer.

antiDrift.charactersNote: A short persona reminder is re-injected deep in long conversations (not only at the top) to fight personality drift.

memoryArchitecture.tier1Core: Always-in-context block (persona essentials + user profile), user-editable, kept under ~800 tokens, with a pressure warning as it fills.
memoryArchitecture.tier2Recall: Rolling conversation summary — older turns are summarised into the story so far.
memoryArchitecture.tier3Archive: On-device IndexedDB store with small embedding search (meanings as numbers) — retrieves the few most relevant memories per turn. Includes an explicit "Remember that..." capture, a periodic reflection/diary pass, and delete/export controls.
memoryArchitecture.rule: "Remember that..." always writes to the archive with a date, so the user can find and remove it later.

brainRouting.law: One chat interface, swappable brain — never hard-code a model name; model menus change.
brainRouting.local: Small on-device model for private/offline basics (WebLLM-class, 1-1.5B) — FEASIBILITY UNPROVEN inside an immersive WebXR session on Quest hardware; must be spike-tested before relying on it.
brainRouting.cloudMini: Fast cheap cloud model for everyday chat (reference point: GPT-4o mini class at roughly $0.36 per 1,000 companion turns at Oct 2026 listed rates).
brainRouting.cloudStrong: Strong cloud model for deep coding and map-design work (roughly 17x the mini cost per turn at listed rates).
brainRouting.userAsset: The owner already holds a Grok (SpaceXSI / xAI) developer account with $20 prepaid API credits (added Oct 29, 2026) — a ready cloud-brain option for the bots and a candidate for QuestBuddi.
brainRouting.fineTuning: None in v1. Prompt persona first, memory second, fine-tune/LoRA-per-persona only if scripted test conversations show a measured consistency gap.
